source.title: The Farmer's Dog ad, as broken down by Peter Kell
source.note: Times are positions in Peter Kell's public short, where the ad plays between his comments. No frame, sound or text of the ad is stored in this repository; the structure below is written in our own words.

moments.what: The dog is named in the first line and shown at his worst, before any product.
moments.kept: A named underdog in the first breath, shown at his lowest.
moments.changed: A rescue puppy becomes Gus, a fiddle-leaf fig, and the line is ours.
moments.why: A name makes people care before they know what is being sold; any category with a 'patient' can use it.

moments.what: One line of backstory: how long they have lived together.
moments.kept: One short line of shared history.
moments.changed: Last year becomes two springs ago.
moments.why: Time together raises the stakes without slowing the opening.

moments.what: The problem is told as a list of household costs, one shot per item.
moments.kept: Three concrete costs, one cut per spoken item.
moments.changed: Sleepless nights and ruined rugs become brown spots, fallen leaves and a water ring on a landlord's rug.
moments.why: Specific damage is believable; 'struggling' on its own is not.

moments.what: The narrator clears the dog of blame.
moments.kept: The owner takes the side of the underdog.
moments.changed: Same beat, held on a hand under one leaf.
moments.why: It moves the blame to the old routine, which is what the product replaces.

moments.what: Failed fixes are named one by one, then dismissed.
moments.kept: Named failed fixes, a cut on each, then one line of defeat.
moments.changed: Foods, supplements and vet visits become misting, a grow light and three different pots.
moments.why: Each failed fix answers 'why not just do X' before the viewer asks it.

moments.what: The product arrives as a discovery, at the door.
moments.kept: Discovery line, then the product on the doorstep.
moments.changed: A food box becomes a Mossbell planter box.
moments.why: The product enters as the turn of the story, not as a pitch.

moments.what: One plain line on how the product works.
moments.kept: One mechanism line in everyday words.
moments.changed: Fresh food delivered becomes watering from below with a dial.
moments.why: One concrete reason it works is enough at this length.

moments.what: The change is shown on the same dog in new places.
moments.changed: No timing or health claim: we show a new leaf.
moments.why: A fictional brand has no customer results to quote.

moments.what: The ask speaks to anyone with the same problem, then gives the offer.
moments.kept: An ask aimed at anyone with the same problem, then the offer.
moments.changed: First-order discount becomes free shipping on the first planter (fictional offer).
moments.why: The ask names the viewer's own situation.

moments.what: The dog's name signs off the ad.
moments.kept: The character's name signs off the ad.
moments.why: The name comes back at the end, so the opening line pays off.

commentary.quote: So right away, we're going straight into a story.
There's like an edit every single second
